thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street's Rebound Shorted Out By Fresh Trade Threats

title: Close Update: Wall Street's Rebound Shorted Out By Fresh Trade Threats
text:
Close Update: Wall Street's Rebound Shorted Out By Fresh Trade Threats September 07, 2018, 04:36:43 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Weighed down by escalating trade tensions between the US and China and rising wage inflation, Wall Street's major market averages closed lower Friday with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite extending their losing streak to a fourth day.
The Dow ended the week 0.2% lower while the S&P 500 lost 1.1% from last week's close and the Nasdaq was down 2.5% amid a tech sector sell-off that was triggered by Facebook ( FB ) COO Sheryl Sandberg and Twitter ( TWTR ) CEO Jack Dorsey's appearance before the Senate Intelligence Committee.
Stocks were trading lower before the opening bell as faster-than-expected August average hourly earnings raised the risk for a more restrictive Federal Reserve. Coupled with concerns that a new trade war front was opening with Japan as well as the lingering rift with China, the Nasdaq and S&P 500 were lower for a fourth day with the tech sector again leading decliners.
President Trump's warning of additional tariffs against Chinese imports shorted out a tech-fueled rebound midday. Speaking to reporters on Air Force One, Trump warned that in addition to $200 billion, another $267 billion in tariffs were "all set to go."
A second rebound materialized later in the day to trim the day's losses but evaporated after Apple ( AAPL ) warned that Chinese trade restrictions would detrimentally impact margins.
In Friday's corporate news, Tesla ( TSLA ) continues to lose ground as the latest debacle from CEO Elon Musk and more high-level defections drives shares another 6% lower. Musk was on-camera allegedly smoking marijuana and drinking alcohol during a radio interview, raising concerns about his fitness as the company's chief executive.
